title: A kiloparsec-scale ordered magnetic field in a galaxy at z = 5.6
question: Are kiloparsec-scale ordered magnetic fields already present in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at z=5.6, as traced by polarised dust emission?

data.angular_resolution: 0.38 x 0.3 arcsec (2.3 x 1.8 kpc at z = 5.6) in the final full-Stokes images
data.sensitivity: 1 sigma RMS 12 uJy/beam (clean stopping level); polarised-intensity RMS 8.5 uJy/beam

recipe.method: Standard pipeline calibration of XX and YY, split, then polarisation calibration with J0423-0120 as polarisation calibrator to correct leakage
key_parameters: Bandpass J0519-4546; phase J0253-5441; flux J0519-4546 (about 5 percent uncertainty)
Parallactic angle coverage wider than 120 degrees in both sessions

recipe.goal: Image Stokes I cubes (line search) and full Stokes continuum images
recipe.method: tclean: hogbom natural-weighted Stokes I cubes to search lines; clarkstokes natural-weighted full Stokes images, cleaned to 12 uJy/beam
key_parameters: Stop at 1 sigma RMS of 12 uJy/beam; beam 0.38 x 0.3 arcsec; polarised-intensity RMS 8.5 uJy/beam

recipe.goal: Reduce and image the archival [C II] data
recipe.method: scriptForPI reduction in CASA 4.2.2, uvcontsub (fitorder = 1), natural-weighted tclean in CASA 6.2.1, channels binned to 100 km/s
key_parameters: Natural weighting instead of the robust weighting of the earlier paper

recipe.goal: Derive polarisation fraction and magnetic-field position angle on a Nyquist grid
recipe.method: Resample Stokes maps with apertures of half the clean beam; per-sample median I, Q, U; P = sqrt(Q^2+U^2)/I; mask P/sigma_P < 3; chi_B = 0.5 arctan(U/Q) + pi/2
key_parameters: Aperture = half the clean beam; P/sigma_P < 3 masked before position-angle calculation
assumptions: Projected B-field is perpendicular to the dust polarisation angle (pi/2 offset)

recipe.goal: Reconstruct the source-plane dust and polarised emission with a pixellated lens model
recipe.method: Pixellated lensing reconstruction (Warren & Dye) with publicly available software; central r < 0.05 arcsec and outer r > 0.18 arcsec masked
software: publicly available lens-reconstruction software (cite: Nightingale2015; Nightingale2021; Dye2018; Dye2022), name not given
key_parameters: Mask r < 0.05 arcsec and r > 0.18 arcsec; best-fit lens parameters in a table

recipe.method: Compare the spatial distribution of polarisation with [C II] kinematics and channel maps
key_parameters: Median velocity dispersion of 140 km/s in the region with polarisation

recipe.goal: Compare polarisation fraction with local starbursts and 9io9
recipe.method: Compare measured fraction at 131 um (~700 pc) with SALSA HAWC+ 154 um results and 9io9

recipe.goal: Test the alpha-Omega disk dynamo via the dynamo number
recipe.method: D_d ~ 9 (h Omega/sigma)^2 ~ 9 (h/r_max)^2 (v_max/sigma)^2 compared with critical value ~7
key_parameters: r_max about 1.5 kpc from the lens model; h = 300 pc; h/r_max ~0.2
assumptions: Velocity gradient solely produced by a galactic disk (most extreme case)

recipe.goal: Estimate an equipartition upper limit on the turbulent magnetic field
recipe.method: B_eq = sqrt(4 pi rho) sigma_v with rho from 50 cm^-3 and [C II] dispersion 140 km/s
key_parameters: [C II] line dispersion 140 km/s at the polarised region; density 50 cm^-3
assumptions: Turbulence dominates the line width; equipartition between turbulent kinetic and magnetic energy

score_reason: Both datasets are ALMA project data and key numeric results (median P, chi_B peaks, amplification, D_d, B_eq) are stated with formulas, but spw setup, tclean parameters, polarisation-calibration scripts and lens-model settings are missing.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA archive links both projects to the paper and the headline numbers (median P 0.9 percent, chi_B peaks 28/78 deg, D_d 2.3, B_eq <= 450 uG) are numeric; the polarisation measurement can be redone with CASA, though the lens reconstruction needs assumptions.
